about: Verity Live Reaction is a 3D yellow emoji-style ball sitting on a blocky Minecraft wooden floor, with a sky and grass in the corner and the game's crosshair just under its chin. The face is drawn with tired, droopy eyes and a small downturned frown, a look of quiet dread rather than shock. That understated misery is the whole point: it is the face of someone watching something go wrong in real time and being unable to do anything about it. It is posted with a "live reaction" style caption to show how you felt the moment you read a message, saw a score, or realized what you had just done.
usage:
The top box describes the moment: "me reading the code review", "me checking my bank app", "when the teacher says 'pop quiz'". The bottom box is usually just "live reaction" or a short label like "live footage", letting the defeated little face carry the punchline.

It works best for slow-burn disappointment rather than big disasters: small, quiet moments of dread like a low battery warning, a long voice note from your boss or the ranked match you just threw. Keep the setup specific and relatable so the reaction feels earned.
ideas: me checking my bank app after the weekend
my team after conceding in the 90th minute
when the creeper sneaks up behind you
